faq.a: Janat is associated with the Arabic form جنات, whose core sense is gardens; gardens of paradise.

faq.q: What is the origin of Janat?
faq.a: Janat is associated with Arabic. Janat is Arabic جَنَّات (Jannāt) 'gardens; gardens of paradise', the plural of جَنَّة (janna). The source gloss 'Garden of Paradise' is broadly consistent. Same name as janaat and jannat.

faq.q: What does Janat mean in Persian?

faq.a: Romanization variants include Janat, janat. Script forms are جنات, जन्नत.

faq.q: Is Janat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
